title: Dyspepsia and Helicobacter pylori: Test-and-Treat and Urgent Endoscopy Triggers

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with dyspepsia in primary care: empirical proton pump inhibitor, Helicobacter pylori testing and eradication, retesting and review, using NICE CG184 and NHS omeprazole information.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Doses of proton pump inhibitors and eradication antibiotics are in appendix tables of NICE CG184 that were not captured; the NHS omeprazole page gives no mg doses.
Alarm features requiring urgent endoscopy were not captured in the extract; apply the NICE recommendations on referral for suspected cancer.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Empirical full-dose proton pump inhibitor (PPI) is offered for 4 weeks in dyspepsia. Stop PPI for 2 weeks before testing for Helicobacter pylori. Test using a carbon-13 urea breath test or a stool antigen test. First-line eradication is a 7-day twice-daily course of PPI with amoxicillin plus clarithromycin or metronidazole, choosing the lowest acquisition cost; second line uses the other antibiotic. NSAIDs should be avoided where possible.

clinicalManagement.title: Empirical PPI
actions: Offer full-dose PPI for 4 weeks; use H2-receptor antagonist if the response is inadequate.

clinicalManagement.title: Test for H. pylori
actions: Carbon-13 urea breath test or stool antigen test.

clinicalManagement.title: Eradicate
actions: PPI plus amoxicillin plus clarithromycin or metronidazole twice daily; second line uses the other antibiotic.

clinicalManagement.title: Retest and review
actions: Retest after treatment for peptic ulcer; annual review for long-term dyspepsia.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
clinicalManagement.timeframe: If second line fails or alarm features

medicationPlan.note: NICE CG184 gives the regimen as proton pump inhibitor twice daily with amoxicillin and clarithromycin or metronidazole for 7 days, with the second-line course using the other antibiotic, but doses are in appendix tables that were not captured; the NHS omeprazole page states omeprazole is usually taken once or twice daily with no mg doses. Prescribe doses from the hospital eradication protocol and product information. Omeprazole may not be suitable in kidney or liver conditions or osteoporosis; long-term use is linked to low vitamin B12 and weakened bones. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
